statements.status_notes: CVE-2025-5278: GNU coreutils sort can read before the start of its heap buffer in begfield() when a key is given in the traditional +POS format with a very large character offset, which can crash sort or expose memory (https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2025-5278, https://debbugs.gnu.org/cgi/bugreport.cgi?bug=78507). Upstream fixed it in src/sort.c with https://github.com/coreutils/coreutils/commit/8c9602e3a145e9596dc1a63c6ed67865814b6633 (begfield and limfield now check the remaining length before advancing the pointer); Debian lists trixie's 9.7-3 as unfixed. The DHI coreutils packages for Debian 13 are rebuilds of Debian's coreutils 9.7-3 with that change backported, and the DHI Debian repository publishes two such builds on amd64 and arm64. Tested in all four packages with the upstream regression test (sort +0.18446744073709551615R on a two-line file, with _POSIX2_VERSION=200809, under valgrind): the DHI sort reports no invalid read and sorts the input, while Debian's own coreutils 9.7-3 on the same systems reports an invalid read. The changelog shipped in both builds records the backport. Every published build carries the fix, so the range ends at the lower of the two.
